questions.:question/problem:
Determine the graph of the following parametrically defined curve:

$$
x=t(t-2),\qquad y=t(t+2),\qquad -2\leq t\leq 2.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Create a table of paired coordinates. First calculate the $x$-values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $8$ | $3$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| $y$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now calculate the $y$-values at the same parameter values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $8$ | $3$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $3$ | $8$ |

The successive points are $(8,0)$, $(3,-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(-1,3)$ and $(0,8)$. Both coordinates turn within the interval: $x=(t-1)^2-1$ has minimum $-1$ at $t=1$, while $y=(t+1)^2-1$ has minimum $-1$ at $t=-1$. Plot a smooth curve through the paired points in parameter order. It dips below the $x$-axis through $(3,-1)$, passes through the origin, then bends left of the $y$-axis through $(-1,3)$ before reaching $(0,8)$. All five choices share the endpoints and the origin, so those three checkpoints alone cannot decide the answer. Check both interior bends.
